modelSelection.reason: Independent acceptance crosses Better Auth ownership, permanent deletion, actual D1/R2 non-atomic failure windows, active-task guards and release eligibility. Sol/high is appropriate for counterexample design and evidence reconciliation.
modelSelection.escalationCondition: Only repeated, concrete reasoning insufficiency after narrowing the case and supplying missing evidence. Permission, environment, network and dependency issues do not justify escalation.

matrix.case: Narrow one-shot R2 delete failure through wrapper around actual local bucket; all other calls delegate to real R2/D1.

Owner GET cannot yield bytes while metadata is pending; real retry tolerates missing R2 objects, marks deleted and completes audit. This is partial-failure convergence, not image restoration.

matrix.expected: Failure window is named and real; no FakeD1/FakeR2-only proof, no accidental other-workspace deletion, queue enqueue or credit mutation. Auth-session maintenance excluded explicitly from business digest if necessary.

matrix.case: Generate a second environment with a new runId; stop local services and dispose Miniflare; retain sanitized original reports and manifest hashes.
matrix.expected: Fresh run proves test regeneration; never recreate same asset IDs or reset deleted status to claim product recovery. Reports contain no session cookies, magic links or credentials; private D1 remains temporary and is not committed. productionLifecycleCovered=false, qualityEvidence=false, modelCallsExecuted=0.

risks.detail: Null expiration semantics differ in current source: asset GET treats null as expired, while lib/releases/repository.ts availability expression treats null as available. This is a source-level risk requiring a candidate-time reproduction, not a confirmed candidate failure or PASS.

Expiry selection compares stored timestamp strings while GET uses Date.parse and release uses julianday. Canonical fixture timestamps must be declared; malformed values and exact clock boundaries must not be inferred from ordinary future dates.

R2 and D1 deletion are not atomic. Object absence after a D1 marking failure must be distinguished from metadata deletion and audit completion; retry convergence does not recover permanently removed images.

Analysis/batch SKU protection is based on every product_reference_versions link; account-assets and retention cleanup do not apply that exclusion. Tests must match these actual scoped contracts rather than assume a universal SKU protection rule.

Immediate deletion guards inspect selected analysis/batch or workspace status before deleting. Shared assets may be referenced elsewhere; include shared-reference controls and report guard scope. Do not claim protection against concurrent worker races from sequential 409 tests.

Deletion attempts are recorded before the deletion try block; audit-insert or audit-completion failures are distinct from the two required injected failures. If encountered, preserve their actual windows and escalate minimal reproduction rather than collapse them into successful cleanup.
Account-assets DELETE has no target ID and currently ignores request body. Isolation must be proven by selected rows and object inventory, not by expecting a forged-body schema error.
A route denial and unchanged D1 count alone are insufficient: verify valid existing objects, all relevant business table rows, deletion audit, credits/usage, queue and R2 keys/hash before and after.

evidencePlan.baseline: Exact candidate SHA and clean candidate files; original developer failures and final report hashes.
evidencePlan.storage: Sanitized asset manifest, real D1 row snapshots and scoped digests, R2 key inventories plus content hashes.
evidencePlan.route: Method/path class, actor alias, target alias/existence, status/error, expiry clock, summary, unchanged-state proof; never log cookies or magic links.
evidencePlan.failure: Injected operation and one-shot boundary, original error summary, object state, asset state, audit status and real retry result.
evidencePlan.ui: Only if required by candidate evidence; use CUA and label actual component plus fixture transport separately from authenticated browser E2E.

stopConditions: Candidate SHA absent: preparation only, no PASS.
Runtime defect: report minimal reproduction, severity and exact files; QA does not fix shared code or weaken assertions.
Same substantive failure twice or one hour without progress: narrow scope and report to controller.
Production, customer, payment, model or credential operations would be required: outside current local QA contract.
nextAction: Wait for controller to fix and dispatch exact JRN-04 candidate SHA and original evidence, then independently execute the scoped acceptance matrix.
